newsitem.title: CUBA: U.S. donors send hurricane aid plane to Cuba.
newsitem.headline: U.S. donors send hurricane aid plane to Cuba.

text.p: Donors in the United States, mostly Cuban Americans, sent a planeload of food aid to Cuba on Saturday for victims of Hurricane Lili, which swept the island a week ago.

Witnesses said the Boeing 707, chartered from the Bolivian airline Lloyd Aereo Boliviano, arrived in Havana in the early evening. Cuban authorities refused to allow foreign journalists to watch the plane being unloaded.
The U.S. government earlier this week waived a ban on direct flights from the United States to the communist-ruled island in order to allow the plane to travel.
The aid, mostly donated by Cuban Americans, was channelled through the Roman Catholic Church in Miami.

An official at the Miami Diocese, Peter Coats, said in Miami earlier on Saturday the church had ready some 70,000 pounds (32,000 kg) of milk powder, rice and beans to send to the island. The group plans to send another flight to Cuba next week.
The aid will be distributed by the Cuban Catholic charity Caritas.

The issue of sending aid to Cuba sparked a sometimes angry debate among Cuban Americans in Miami this week, with some saying any aid would not go to hurricane victims but would just be used by President Fidel Castro's government.
Hurricane Lili destroyed more than 5,000 homes and damaged crops, power lines and communications in central and western areas of Cuba.

Mexico has sent two planeloads of food and roofing material and the Spanish government has sent some $200,000 worth of aid. Cuba has also appealed to the United Nations for emergency humanitarian assistance.
